These questions exist only while the counter is open, which is the sequencing trap, an eval set started after September 15 2026 with no capture in between can't exist before May 2027.

next.item: The Counter Copilot, phase two, staff-facing only. A retrieval assistant over their own bounded corpus answering policy and procedure with the source page cited and a visible I don't know where the corpus is silent, with a deterministic calculator alongside it computing every number in code. It never talks to a customer, it refuses anything weather or flyability shaped, and it refuses the NPS check-in then weigh gear then pay sequence because that is an ordered regulated intake a novice must not be told wrong.
next.metric: Scored against the captured eval set before it goes anywhere live, then measured at the April spin-up as counter contacts handled per staffed hour by a first-season hire against the prior season. Any answer with no source is suppressed rather than generated, and the suppression rate is reported as a number rather than hidden. The 14 percent average and 34 percent novice figures from the 5,179 agent study are the mechanism we expect to transfer, never the magnitude we promise.

next.item: A discovery session on the actual booking and quoting surface behind the counter for climbers and charters, which nobody has verified and which we refuse to guess at, followed by a deterministic quote engine with no model anywhere in it, a tracked pipeline, and a human hitting send on every quote. Seven of the eight fields on their own reservation form are already structured, so version one parses nothing.
next.metric: A written answer on what actually runs behind the counter today, plus a counted volume and turnaround for expedition, charter, river and sling inquiries. No estimate hardens before both exist. Once built, the engine is measured on quote turnaround time and on arithmetic errors per hundred quotes against the published fee table. The gear worksheet emits billable weight against the 125 pound allowance and nothing that resembles a load sheet.

later.item: The Part 135 safety management system, carried as a question to ask and not as a gap we claim. Trade press reported in April 2024 that charter operators have up to three years to implement a proactive safety system. Nothing we fetched describes where Talkeetna Air Taxi stands on it, so we ask. We are also not the right people to build it, and no build for it is on offer here.
later.metric: An answer on the call, either way. No build attached, no gap asserted, because asserting one on an unfetched page would be inventing a need.

later.item: Watch what their own booking vendor's assistant is permitted to say in their name. FareHarbor announced a guest communication assistant on April 27 2026, still rolling out to a select group of operators with no named customers, outcomes or pricing published. We are not selling a guest-facing assistant here and we think nobody should sell them one.
later.metric: A reviewed decision each season on which questions the vendor's assistant may answer in their name, with is it flying today off that list. The risk worth watching is a channel they do not control answering the one question their reputation rests on keeping human, under a 100 percent refund policy they pay for.

later.item: The April spin-up itself. A counter that re-staffs every spring is permanently new to the fact set, which is the multiplier sitting under the copilot rather than a product of its own. No fetched page describes a recruiting bottleneck, so a hiring tool would be an invented need and is not proposed.
later.metric: Time for a first-season counter person to answer the common question set unaided, tracked against the previous April once the record and the copilot exist.

later.item: Weather-day walk-offs. Count how often a party stands down and how many seats it involves. Count it, do not automate it. Nothing verified says how often this happens or how many seats are at stake, so no standby, waitlist or seat recovery automation is proposed here, with or without AI.
later.metric: A tallied count of walk-offs and seats per staffed week, which either turns this into a real question later or retires it honestly. Their unconditional 100 percent refund is a competitive asset, more generous than either published competitor policy, and it is not something to touch.

later.item: The go/no-go call stays exactly where it is, with a person, at check-in, handed to the customer after a verbal briefing on visibility and current conditions. It appears on this list so it is on the record as protected rather than pending.
later.metric: Zero model-generated flyability verdicts in anything we build, permanently. The independent 2025 benchmark of 147,182 images across 444 FAA camera sites found no model reaching the FAA accuracy threshold, best average error about 1.8 statute miles, and the handoff of that decision to the customer is the product rather than the bottleneck.

later.item: Several parts of this business have nothing worth selling, and saying so plainly is the useful answer. The 8 AM and 8 PM channel 1 broadcast and the basecamp voice relay are limited by connectivity on a glacier rather than by software. Weight and balance, load planning, dispatch and maintenance records are regulated flight operations and stay where they are. No usable review data could be opened, so no reputation or content work is proposed. No language switcher was found on any of the three operator sites checked and no verified claim establishes an international share, so no translation work either.
later.metric: No metric, and that is the finding. The measurable outcome is money not spent, and the map is complete rather than quietly trimmed.

roadmap.gates: Five gates, each earned by something that will genuinely have been measured by the time it is checked, and each one framed as their off-ramp rather than ours. GATE 0, before anything at all is bought. One week of tally marks at the desk before September 15 2026, producing a count of day-of conditions contacts and hours or price questions per staffed day. If that count sits below the break-even figure the study prints, phase one is not worth buying and we will say so in writing. This gate costs them a notepad and it is the only gate that comes before any money moves. GATE 1, before the Conditions Board is committed. The one day camera coverage check and the hosting or DNS confirmation both come back written. If the usable cameras look at the valley rather than the routes, or the /denali-webcam/ path can't be recovered, the Facts Spine ships alone and the board narrows or drops. They keep a working single source of truth either way. GATE 2, before phase two is funded at all. The tally week re-run in the same week of the 2027 season, against the 2026 baseline. Said plainly, if phase one does not move the tallied contact count, phase two does not get funded. That is not a formality and it is not renegotiated afterwards. They keep the record and the live page and owe nothing further. GATE 3, two conditions and both are required before the Counter Copilot is built. One, the record held single-sourced through a full off season with a named owner and dated last-reviewed stamps, verified by re-audit at the April spin-up. Two, an eval set of real counter questions with human-labelled correct answers captured from a live season, which is why the notepad starts in 2026 rather than after a contract. Volume decides whether the copilot is worth it, the corpus and the eval set decide whether it works, and only the second pair blocks. GATE 4, on the expedition and charter desk. No estimate hardens and no work is sold before a discovery session establishes what actually runs behind the counter today and a counted inquiry volume exists. The structural gap in their form is verified, the size of the prize is not, and we will not price against an unknown integration surface. Every gate is measured against something already being collected by the time it is read, and no gate rests on a number nobody is counting.
high_integrity_dates: September 15 2026, a hard commitment because it is theirs rather than ours. The 2026 staffed season closes and the tally week has to be finished before it. Miss it and the 2026 baseline does not exist, the before and after slides to 2028, and the eval set capture loses a whole season of real questions.

The content working session happens between September 16 2026 and March 31 2027, deliberately outside May 1 to September 15, because the counter can't give a working session in the middle of a staffed season and that is when the person who owns these facts is least available.

Live and shaken out before the last half of April 2027. This is the one hard commitment we make on our own work in this roadmap. Pilots sit one week of ground school in Talkeetna in the last half of April and the counter spins up behind them, so anything not live and settled by then misses a whole operating year. A build landing in June is a build that missed 2027.
Nothing else in this roadmap carries a date. Every other item is sequenced by confidence and by what has actually been measured, and none of it should be read as a calendar promise.

roi.cost_note: Five-year total cost of ownership for phase one, not sticker price, and the ask is deliberately staged so the owner can stop after Stage A. FIXED-PRICE BUILD, 24,000 dollars total for roughly 4.5 person-weeks, split into Stage A at 9,500 (the Facts Spine, one structured record per published fact, every page rendering from it, plus the FAA camera coverage check and the hosting or DNS check the feasibility audit made binding, plus the tally protocol) and Stage B at 14,500 (the Conditions Board on the /denali-webcam/ path). Fixed price means the person-week overrun risk sits with us rather than with them, so implementation carries no scenario padding, which is why the same 24,000 appears in all three scenarios. IMPLEMENTATION AND INTEGRATION is the whole of that line because there is no licence and no subscription to buy. TRAINING AND CHANGE MANAGEMENT, stated in hours rather than called included, 16 hours of our facilitation (an 8 hour content working session, a 4 hour counter walkthrough, a 4 hour pre-season refresh) plus 16 hours of their staff time (10 hours of GM and office manager time, 6 hours across counter staff), their hours priced at an ASSUMED loaded rate because no wage figure is verified anywhere. The working session is scheduled outside May 1 to September 15. ONGOING RUN COST, 1,800 dollars a year at the most-likely figure, covering hosting, feed monitoring and the timestamp-based camera health check, one content review pass a year with a dated last-reviewed stamp per fact, and repair when an FAA camera endpoint moves. There is NO inference or token line, no model monitoring line, no evaluation line and no human-in-the-loop review line, because phase one contains no model. That absence is the largest single reason this run cost is small, and it is the honest reason, not a discount. CONTINGENCY of 15 to 20 percent is still applied even against a fixed price, because the reserve exists for the organisational failure modes, a working session that slips, a fact nobody can decide, a second content pass, not for our engineering.

benefits.benefit: Flightseeing seats retained on marginal-weather mornings, where a customer who can see the mountain on their phone decides to come in rather than stand down
benefits.basis: THE ONLY LINE IN THE PAYBACK ARITHMETIC, and it is presented as a BREAK-EVEN, never as a projection. Unit price is anchored to a verified figure, the published Southside Explorer adult fare of 275 dollars, which is the LOWEST adult tour fare on their own product pages and already net of the 7.5 percent Federal Transportation Tax and 3 percent Borough Tax they publish separately. Contribution per retained seat is ASSUMED at 50 percent of that fare in the conservative case. The volume driver, seats retained per staffed day, is ASSUMED across a deliberately wide range because it has never been measured, which is exactly why it is run as a break-even and handed to the owner as a test.
benefits.note: The direction is set by the feasibility audit. Under an unconditional 100 percent refund a false Flying creates no new refund liability while a false Down or a stale Holding converts a paid seat into a refund plus a seat that can no longer be sold. That asymmetry is why the value sits on the imagery half of the board, and why NO return is modelled on the counter-flipped status field, whose deflection is negatively correlated with need.

benefits.benefit: Counter minutes recovered on day-of conditions contacts, the calls their own FAQ manufactures by telling customers to call the day they fly
benefits.basis: Computed from ASSUMED contacts per staffed day, an ASSUMED deflection share, ASSUMED minutes per contact and an ASSUMED loaded hourly cost, against a staffed-day count modelled from the verified May 1 to September 15 window and the verified 7 AM to 7 PM staffing. Every one of those four drivers is assumed, and no verified call volume figure exists anywhere in this package.
benefits.note: CAPACITY, NOT CASH, and it never converts. No hire is deferred, no backfill is avoided and nobody is redeployed, because the role verified on their own careers page already stacks greeting, check-in, payments, phone, reservations, email and online bookings on one person. Computed and printed SEPARATELY and never added to the cash line. State the result plainly even though it is unflattering to us, counter minutes at any believable contact volume recover only 2 to 47 percent of five-year TCO, so anyone who sells this operator a tool on hours-saved arithmetic is selling a number their own staffed-day count will not support. The vendor formula in the research is exactly that pattern, monthly visitors times 0.015 times 4.5 minutes, an estimate presented as a measurement.

benefits.benefit: One verified defect repaired, three pages publishing three different staffed-hours answers collapse to one
benefits.basis: QUARANTINED FROM THE FORMULA AT ZERO DOLLARS. The defect is verified across three separately fetched pages. What is not verified is how often a customer acts on the wrong one, so it carries no modelled dollar and it stays out of the arithmetic.
benefits.note: This is the reason Stage A is worth buying at zero deflection. Fixing something already known to be wrong needs no volume estimate to justify, and it is the hard prerequisite for everything in the Next lane. The residual risk is named rather than hidden, single sourcing propagates a mistake everywhere at once, handled by one named owner and a dated last-reviewed stamp per fact.

benefits.benefit: A measured 2026 baseline that gates every later dollar, taken with a notepad in the weeks the season has left
benefits.basis: QUARANTINED FROM THE FORMULA AT ZERO DOLLARS. Its value is decision quality rather than a cash flow. One week of tally marks at the desk before September 15 2026 produces the contact-volume figure that this entire package lacks, and it costs nothing but attention.
benefits.note: This is the honest reason a low-five-figure phase one is the right size of ask. If the tally comes back small, the correct answer is that Stage B is not worth buying, and we would rather write that sentence than sell around it.

roi.benefit_phasing: No day-one benefit anywhere, and here seasonality bites harder than the usual ninety-day stabilisation. The build lands in the shoulder season and the clock only runs during the 138 staffed days between May 1 and September 15, so a slip past mid-April costs a whole year rather than a quarter. Year one is a partial season at an ASSUMED ramp of 30 percent conservative, 40 percent most likely and 55 percent aggressive. That ramp is doing two jobs, the usual shakeout of a new page against real traffic, and an awareness curve, because a conditions page nobody knows about deflects nothing in its first weeks. Year two is the first full run-rate season. Year three onward is flat rather than compounding, and that is deliberate. There is no network effect and no learning loop in a static page reading public feeds, so claiming compounding here would be inventing a curve.

scenarios.conservative: SCOPE THIS SENTENCE CAREFULLY. The conservative case for the FULL phase one, both stages, DOES NOT CLEAR. At an assumed 0.25 retained seats per staffed day it recovers 44 percent of five-year TCO and never crosses cumulative cost inside the horizon. We are saying that in the study rather than tuning a driver until it goes away. WHAT THE CONSERVATIVE CASE DOES CLEAR is the RECOMMENDED ask, which is smaller than the full build. Stage A at 9,500 dollars fixed, priced honestly as decision data plus one verified defect repaired, clears on its own terms with no volume estimate in it anywhere. Stage B is not committed at signature, it is released only if the owner's own tally week puts him above the break-even line the study prints.
scenarios.most_likely: Clears, on assumptions that are still assumptions. 0.50 retained seats per staffed day, which is one seat every other staffed day, at 180 dollars contribution. Recovers 133 percent of five-year TCO with payback in month 45, which is late in the horizon rather than early, and that is what a small fixed-price build against an unmeasured volume should look like. Read this as the middle of a wide band, not as a forecast.
scenarios.aggressive: Clears comfortably and should be treated as the ceiling of the band rather than the target. 1.00 retained seat per staffed day at 220 dollars contribution recovers 362 percent with payback in month 19. Nothing in this package establishes that this case is the true one, and the spread between it and the conservative case is the honest measure of how little anyone currently knows about the volume.

roi.conservative_clears_scope: SCOPED, AND THE SCOPE MUST SURVIVE INTO THE PAGE. The full 24,000 dollar phase one does NOT clear its conservative case. The RECOMMENDED ASK, Stage A at 9,500 dollars priced as decision data plus one verified defect repaired, does. Stage B is released by their own measured week, not at signature.
roi.payback_range: Reported as a range and computed in code, never as a point. At the conservative seat-retention assumption there is NO PAYBACK INSIDE THE FIVE-YEAR HORIZON and 44 percent of TCO is recovered. At the most-likely assumption payback lands in month 45. At the aggressive assumption it lands in month 19. The break-even sits between 0.50 and 0.75 retained seats per staffed day on the most expensive honest cost stack, which is roughly one retained seat every other staffed day. The counter-minutes ladder recovers 2 to 47 percent of TCO across the same three cases and never pays back, which is the most useful number in the section because it rebuts the hours-saved arithmetic this industry is sold.
roi.base_rate_note: The outside view first, stated straight. Most AI pilots show no P&L impact, MIT put it at about 95 percent and RAND at about 80 percent of AI projects failing, and the population evidence for this specific industry runs the same way, a March 2026 survey of 505 tour and activity operators found 56 percent still finding AI tools overwhelming and 44 percent reporting they had received inaccurate or misleading information from them. The unusual thing here has to be said precisely rather than used as a free pass. PHASE ONE CONTAINS NO MODEL, so the model-specific half of that base rate does not apply to it, no hallucination, no eval debt, no drift, no inference cost, no retrieval failure. That is a real exemption and it is narrow. The OTHER half, which is the larger half, applies in full, because most of those failures are organisational rather than technical, no owner, no measured baseline, no workflow embedding, thin adoption, scope creep. This design attacks those four directly. It is workflow-embedded because it sits on the exact contact their own published FAQ manufactures. It is adoption-owned because a named person owns the number and because the half the ROI rests on needs no human action at all. It is measured because the baseline is taken BEFORE the build with a notepad. Its degraded state is its safest property, the board auto-expires to their own existing FAQ sentence, so a failed board equals today rather than something worse. Removing the model removes the most-cited cause of failure and it also removes any claim to an AI premium, which is why the ask is small and why saying so is the pitch.
roi.value_owner: Courtney Shaffer, General Manager, named on their own team page since 2017, owns the number. She is the right owner for a structural reason rather than a seniority one, the Facts Spine does not need data found, it needs a fact DECIDED, and the staffed-hours contradiction can only be resolved by someone with authority to say which answer is true. She owns one dated last-reviewed stamp per fact and the annual pre-season content pass. The office manager owns the daily tally sheet during the measurement weeks. Paul Roderick as Operations Director owns the camera-to-route labelling call, since a clear valley camera is not a clear mountain and only operations can say which site speaks for which route. VARIANCE CHECK, three gates, each comparing actual against a baseline that exists before the spend. Gate one, the 2026 tally week taken before September 15 2026. Gate two, at the end of the 2027 season, the same tally in the same calendar week with the board live, alongside server-side page views which are counted rather than asserted. Gate three, that 2027 variance gates any phase two commitment. A case with no owner and no post-hoc measurement is fantasy by construction, so if the 2027 comparison comes back flat the correct conclusion is that the board did not pay and the Next lane does not open.
assumptions: VERIFIED, the season window runs May 1 to September 15, quoted from their climbing FAQ.

VERIFIED, the office is staffed 7 AM to 7 PM, quoted from that same climbing FAQ. Their site publishes two other answers for the identical window. We used the narrowest of the three, which is the conservative choice, and repairing that contradiction is itself Stage A's deliverable.
MODELLED, 138 staffed days per season, a calendar count of the verified window.

VERIFIED, the published Southside Explorer adult fare is 275 dollars for the one hour flight and 400 dollars with a glacier landing, and the glacier add-on is 125 dollars per person. We anchored the cash line to the LOWEST of those.
VERIFIED, the published fares are net of the 7.5 percent Federal Transportation Tax and 3 percent Borough Tax the company publishes separately, so no tax is double counted.
VERIFIED, the refund posture is unconditional at 100 percent, which is what makes a false Down the expensive error direction rather than a false Flying.
ASSUMED, contribution per retained seat at 135, 180 and 220 dollars. No cost data exists for this operator.
ASSUMED, retained seats per staffed day at 0.25, 0.50 and 1.00. This is the single driver that moves the answer most and it has never been measured.

ASSUMED, contacts per staffed day at 6, 12 and 24. NO VERIFIED CALL VOLUME FIGURE EXISTS ANYWHERE, and none was inferred from the 981 registered 2026 Denali climbers because their share of those climbers is also unverified.
ASSUMED, deflection share at 20, 30 and 40 percent, applied to the imagery half of the board only.
ASSUMED, minutes per conditions contact at 3, 4 and 5.
ASSUMED, loaded hourly cost of the person at the counter at 28, 32 and 36 dollars. No wage figure for this employer is verified anywhere.
ASSUMED, year-one ramp at 30, 40 and 55 percent.
ASSUMED, no compounding after year two. A static page over public feeds has no learning loop.
QUOTED, implementation at 24,000 dollars fixed, staged 9,500 for the Facts Spine and 14,500 for the Conditions Board.

CONDITION, NOT ASSUMPTION. FAA weather camera coverage for the Ruth, the Kahiltna, Tokositna West, the Root Canal and the Kichatna Spires is UNVERIFIED. It is one day of checking inside Stage A and it happens before Stage B is priced. If coverage is thin the Conditions Board shrinks or dies, and the ROI dies with it.
CONDITION, NOT ASSUMPTION. Hosting or DNS access to recover the /denali-webcam/ path is unconfirmed. Also inside Stage A.
EXCLUDED ON PURPOSE, no benefit is modelled for standby or seat recovery automation, for a guest-facing assistant, or for the counter copilot.

QUALITATIVE AND QUARANTINED, carrying zero dollars in the formula. The counter keeps the go/no-go conversation the business is known for. Their office manager's forecasting judgement is reinforced rather than replaced. Staff onboarding in the last half of April gets easier once one true answer per fact exists.

computed_by_roi_math.break_even_statement: Between 0.50 and 0.75 retained seats per staffed day on the most expensive honest cost stack. Roughly one retained seat every other staffed day.
